messages:
caitlin: Quick kickoff — we need to tighten isolation for the next private deployment wave. Questions: 1) planned RBAC changes (deny by default) — how do we avoid a mass outage when KMS auth or audit-forwarders fail? 2) Minimal netpol whitelist pattern for on-prem where egress is via a proxy. 3) Incident runbook updates for key rotation failures.

dmitri: +1 on deny-by-default. For KMS: add a scoped emergency service-account with explicit allow to decrypt, but lock it behind a manual approval (GitHub PR or oncall approval). Document the exact steps.

ian: Quick note on audit-forwarders — if we can't reach central logging, they should buffer locally and expose a metrics signal (eg: audit_forwarder_stalled). If you see that metric flip, run the fallback to S3 proxy.

nina: For netpol we should use default-deny + minimal egress: only proxy IPs, internal control plane CIDR, and KMS endpoint CIDR. Something like:
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: limited-egress
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.20.0.0/16  # control plane
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.30.1.0/32  # egress-proxy
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```
This keeps things minimal and works with airgapped setups.

caitlin: Good. For RBAC, what about a "break-glass" kubeconfig kept in a sealed location? Ops wants to avoid human firewall bypasses.

dmitri: We can do a break-glass but make it auditable: require an approval ticket and Slack ack, and expire tokens after 1 hour. Also record KMS usage logs for that SA. Put the kubeconfig encrypted with the same KMS key and grant decrypt only via an approval workflow.

security-bot: NOTICE: recent vuln CVE-2026-1453 affecting on-prem KMS agent. Patch v1.2.3 fixes a path traversal during key sync. See https://internal.redwood/security/alerts/2026-1453

nina: Thanks bot — if customers are on older agents, RBAC change could lock them out if agent can't authenticate. We need a preflight that verifies KMS handshake and audit-forwarder connectivity before applying deny-by-default. Add a toggle in the deployment CI: `--require-kms-handshake`

ian: Agreed. Preflight checklist (proposal):
- validate KMS reachable and key ACLs: `kmsctl test-decrypt --key prod/priv-deploy`
- confirm audit-forwarder -> proxy connection: `curl https://proxy.internal/health`
- verify emergency SA decrypt permission exists
- run smoke inference against pinned model to ensure runtime loads keys
If any step fails, abort RBAC rollout and open incident.

caitlin: Incident flow for key-rotation failure? Draft:
1) Pager -> oncall (security + infra)
2) Revoke new key, restore decrypt rights to previous key for emergency SA
3) Roll back RBAC deny if rollout in progress
4) Rotate keys offline, re-provision agent, validate logs
5) Postmortem with timeline + impact metrics (token cost, requests dropped)
Is that too heavy?

dmitri: Looks fine. Add: collect `kube-audit` bundle and KMS agent logs and attach to pager ticket. Also note timeline for key TTLs (some infra rotates keys every 20m, others hourly) — sync expectations.

nina: One more: telemetry / SLOs to add to the Console so customers see isolation health: `kms_handshake_success_rate`, `audit_forwarder_lag_seconds`, `egress_deny_rate`. If any crosses threshold, auto-open a support ticket.

caitlin: Permissions matrix idea: keep three tiers per private deployment: admin (bootstrap ops), service (normal SA), emergency (manual SA). Document the exact verbs for each: admins get `*` in namespace, service accounts get specific list (get/list/watch/exec on pods, secrets:get on sealed-secret-controller), emergency gets decrypt only.

ian: For sealed-secret workflow: ensure sealed secrets are encrypted with customer-specific key and controller only has unwrap permission. That reduces blast radius if an SA is compromised.

security-bot: ACTION: created ticket #SEC-5421 "preflight KMS + audit-forwarder check in deploy pipeline" assigned to dmitri. ETA 48h.

caitlin: Thanks — next steps: dmitri to prototype preflight, nina to update netpol templates, ian to add audit bundle checklist, I'll update runbooks and the RBAC matrix. We'll reconvene after PRs. :thumbsup:

dmitri: I'll drop a draft PR with a `--require-kms-handshake` CI gate and a small `kmsctl` shim. If folks want to test in sandbox, ping me.

nina: I'll add the netpol snippets to docs and include a reference for on-prem proxy IP ranges.

ian: I'll create an incident playbook doc and link it in the runbook.

caitlin: Perfect. Closing loop — thanks team.
